releases.summary: A new panel in the menu bar, and Jumpr can now click itself.
bullets: One panel for everything. Click the J in the menu bar: an on/off switch, a live preview of your labels, label color, letter color, label size, the shortcut, start at login and the update check are all there. The separate Settings window is gone.
Pick colors in place. Choose from swatches or type an exact color. The system color picker is no longer used.
Letters in any color. Letters can be any color you like, or Auto, which picks black or white, whichever reads better on your label color. If you had set a letter color, it is kept.
Jumpr labels itself. Its own menu bar icon gets a label. Type it to open the panel, and every control in the panel gets a label too.
Dia: the folders in the sidebar have labels. Type one to open or close that folder.
Web pages: text a page lets you move to with the keyboard now gets a label, such as the days in a date picker. Days a page marks as unavailable are skipped.
releases.note: Not fixed, because Dia does not tell macOS they are there: the pinned tiles at the top of Dia's sidebar, and the individual spaces in the strip at its bottom (the strip gets one label).

releases.summary: Messages now gets labels on its sidebar.
bullets: Messages: every conversation in the list and every pin has a label. Type it to open that conversation.

Other apps built the same way: text that an app says can be pressed now gets a label, wherever it is. Some of it does nothing when pressed: in Messages, the time stamps between messages get labels too.

releases.summary: A housekeeping release. Nothing you see or do changes.
bullets: The license notice for Sparkle, the updater Jumpr includes, now ships inside the app.
Two debugging hooks are switched off unless Jumpr is started with a debug flag.
Code the app never used is gone.

releases.summary: The menu bar icon is now the J from Jumpr's logo, on its own with no box. It follows your menu bar: white on a dark bar, black on a light one. Nothing else changes.
The menu bar icon is now Jumpr's own yellow J label, matching the app icon and the site. Nothing else changes.
First public release. Press ⌘⇧Space and every clickable thing on every display gets a short label, usually two letters. Type the letters and it clicks.
bullets: Windows, menus, the Dock and menu bar icons
Works in Safari, Chrome and web-based apps
Checks for updates once a day; you can turn that off
Free and open source (MIT). macOS 15 or later. Built for Apple silicon and Intel; the Intel build has not yet been tested on an Intel Mac.
